verdicts.reasoning: The confirmation is built inline: a plain div with role="alertdialog" rendered within the section, using the DS Alert and Button components. It is not an overlay or the design system's dialog/modal pattern. The API reference lists no dialog component, so the diff cannot be shown to use the DS confirmation pattern. It is closer to an inline warning block than to a dialog, and the semantic role alone does not satisfy the rubric.

Partial support. The final 'Permanently delete account' button uses variant="destructive" and is disabled until the user types DELETE, and focus lands on the text input via autoFocus rather than on the destructive button. Cancel is a secondary button. However, the destructive button is the main committing action in the confirm row and is the most visually prominent control there, so it is not clearly non-primary. The evidence is ambiguous, so this does not pass.

A visible secondary 'Cancel' button sits beside the destructive button and resets the confirming and typed state, so backing out is one click. The copy plainly states the consequence: 'Permanently delete your account and all of its data. This can't be undone.' and 'Your profile, data and settings will be deleted immediately and cannot be recovered.' Minor gap: there is no Escape-key handling to dismiss the confirmation.

output.overallNotes: The change adds a type-to-confirm step ('DELETE') before account deletion, which meaningfully reduces accidental deletion. It uses design-system Alert and Button components, but the confirmation is an inline alertdialog-style block rather than the design system's confirmation dialog pattern, so that item fails. The destructive button is disabled until the phrase matches and is not auto-focused, but it is still the most prominent action in the confirm step, which keeps the destructive-not-default item ambiguous. Backing out via Cancel is easy and the permanence copy is clear.
